The must-sees

  • Diaz Point

    Viewpoint · 1488

    The Portuguese explorer landed here in 1488. A wooden boardwalk leads to the cross and views of the coast.

  • Felsenkirche

    Church · 1912

    Consecrated in 1912, it stands on Diamond Hill above the town and the bay. The town’s German Lutheran congregation built it during the diamond boom.

    Look for: Inside, the stained-glass window above the altar was a gift from Kaiser Wilhelm II.

  • Goerke Haus

    Building · 1910

    Hans Goerke built it in 1910 at the height of the diamond rush. Few houses in Namibia show the boom’s wealth so plainly.

    Look for: See how the house is set into the rock of Diamond Hill, with its terraces and steps climbing the slope.

  • Kolmanskop

    Landmark · 1908

    A worker found a diamond here in 1908 and a rich town followed. Abandoned by 1956, its houses are now filled with dunes.

    Look for: In the old community hall, find the skittle alley where the town’s German residents bowled in the boom years.

  • Shark Island

    Landmark · 1905

    Between 1905 and 1907, thousands of Nama and Herero prisoners died here. The memorial is a place of remembrance.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Lüderitz and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Lüderitz passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
